title: Design Diary #1 - All Aboard the Fail Train! Next Stop, the Island of Discarded Game Ideas!
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cfGpIvLPcPw

Daniel (@dungeondive) opens a design diary series about the game he's building, and structures the first episode almost entirely around his failures — a decade of abandoned prototypes laid out on the table.

The inspirations come first: *Talisman* for house-ruleable adventure without a GM, *Mertwig's Maze* for location-specific mini-games, *Runebound* for expansion tails, and *Arkham Horror* for the d6 dice pool he keeps returning to. He explains why the pool works for him — no target-number arithmetic, no power creep, just adding and removing dice, which reads at a glance as "I am good at this" or "I am not."

Then the graveyard. A 2016 hierarchy of world/environment/setting/area/location that collapsed under its own nesting. *Marching Order*, a worker-placement dungeon crawl on a party dashboard, convoluted by shift and action points. A d12 press-your-luck system. *Claymore Quest*. The diagnosis is the episode's most useful moment: he kept hitting design roadblocks and patching them rather than going back to fix the rule that caused them, so he'd finish with a pile of patches instead of a game.

He closes on the current design — an 8.5×11 hex map, nine card decks, four gems, six bosses.

----

Have you ever patched a broken rule rather than redesigning it — and how did that turn out?
